patch_description:
The previous edit failed because of an indentation mismatch in the first SEARCH block. I retry with the exact verbatim text (module-level functions use 4-space indentation, and the trailing helper insertion point differs).

The substantive idea is unchanged: the current program reaches ≈0.96 using only stochastic annealing (`_local_search`), which plateaus around dmin/dmax ≈ 0.48 because decaying jitter repeatedly knocks points off the active constraints. The prior best generation (score 1.00) used a constrained SLSQP polish: maximize t = dmin² subject to d²ᵢⱼ ≥ t and d²ᵢⱼ ≤ 1 (after diameter normalization). This is the exact KKT form of the problem — at the optimum, minimum-distance pairs sit at the boundary of the diameter constraints, which a constrained solver resolves precisely and stochastic search cannot.

Changes:
1. Add a `_ratio_sq` helper computing (dmin/dmax)² directly.
2. Collect the top-3 distinct annealing candidates instead of only the best (the landscape has many near-tied basins, and the constrained polish may lift any of them past the best).
3. For each top-3 candidate, apply σ ∈ {0, 0.05, 0.15, 0.3} symmetry-breaking perturbations and run SLSQP with per-pair closure-built constraint Jacobians (built in a plain loop — the vectorized Jacobian fill from an earlier generation crashed on a shape mismatch, so fancy indexing is deliberately avoided).
4. Trim annealing budgets slightly (2200→1600, 1200→1000, final polish 4000→1500) to keep total runtime bounded while adding the fast SLSQP stage.
